_comment: THE ROLE REGISTRY. A role is a contract, not a model.
Every role used to be an env var pointing at one gateway alias, which made
'which model is the reviewer' a thing you learned by reading a shell script.
It also made the one property the review gate depends on -- that reviewer and
implementer are different models -- invisible and unenforceable.
`model` here is a GATEWAY ALIAS, not a checkpoint. The gateway owns which
weights an alias resolves to and on which card, so a role can be re-pointed at
a different model, quantisation or GPU without touching the loop. That is what
'agent identity is separate from model identity' means in practice.
`may_change` is enforced, not advisory: a role that writes outside its paths
is a role doing someone else's job, which is how a defect gets patched at the
`escalates_to` is the ladder. A role that fails repeatedly does not try
harder; it hands a structured stuck-report to the role named here.
See docs/AGENT-ORGANISATION.md. Roles marked implemented:false are declared
so the pipeline can name them and so the gap is visible -- they are NOT

analyst.owns: repository state, intent, gaps, and the context every other role needs
analyst.note: Deterministic today: reads the source and proposes nothing. That is why it is trusted.

decomposer.owns: goals split into independently achievable tasks, one file each
decomposer.note: One file per task is a hard constraint: apply_proposal writes exactly one, so a two-file task lands half and closes anyway.

product.owns: user stories, requirements, scope, definition of done, success AND kill criteria, acceptance criteria
product.gate: acceptance criteria exist and are satisfied

architect.owns: system boundaries, interfaces, APIs, data models, dependencies, constraints
architect.gate: the design is coherent and its interfaces are stated

implementer.owns: code that satisfies an approved design

reviewer.owns: correctness, quality, maintainability, architectural consistency, regressions
reviewer.note: must_differ_from is ENFORCED at call time by asking the gateway what each alias resolves to. A reviewer that degrades to the implementer's model returns a correlated opinion labelled independent.

test-engineer.owns: unit, integration, regression and system tests
test-engineer.note: The gate exists today as run_repo_gates, but nothing AUTHORS the tests -- the implementer does, which is why a goal asking for behaviour plus tests landed only the behaviour.

doc-engineer.owns: inline, API, architecture, user and developer documentation, examples

ux.applies_when: the project has a user interface

dx.applies_when: the project has a developer-facing surface
dx.owns: APIs, SDKs, CLIs, configuration, error messages, install, debugging, extension points

style.owns: formatting and lint, across every repository
style.note: REPAIRS, never refuses. A style finding is fixed by the repo's own formatter and only an unresolvable disagreement becomes a finding. A pipeline that halts on formatting is a pipeline that does not run.

gates.applies: when the project has a UI
when the project has a developer surface

defect_routing._comment: Which role a finding goes BACK to. A defect patched at the wrong layer is the failure this prevents: an implementer working around an architectural fault produces code that passes every gate and encodes the fault permanently.
